process_area.title: Loan Origination, Disbursement & Inventory Collateral Tracking

value_stream.name: Trade Reseller Floor-Plan & Dealer Inventory Financing

fields.Participants: Dealer, Trade Account Manager, Credit Manager
fields.Trigger: Dealer requests funding for a purchase/stocking order

workflows.name: Dealer Purchase/Floor-Plan Funding Request & Loan Origination

Automation Opportunity: - Online funding request with auto-limit-check, rate-engine, and disclosure generation.
Controls: - CTL-12: separate credit approval from sales; CTL-05 (prevent unauthorized credit-limit overrides); CTL-21 (origination accuracy).
Cross-references: - links to VS-68 (credit), VS-11 (trade/orders), VS-16 (O2C), VS-17 (GL)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Over-limit risk**: funding beyond the dealer's headroom breaches the credit decision; mitigated by a hard limit-check gate in origination.
- **Ineligible-category risk**: funding non-eligible/non-resalable categories weakens collateral; mitigated by category-eligibility check at origination.
System Touchpoints: - Floor-plan origination; limit/headroom check (W5370); rate engine (W5375); RA 3765 disclosure (W5376); GL posting (VS-17).
Time Estimate: - Originations are portal-received and system score-decisioned per the W5370 framework: the Credit Analyst's ~1–2-hour underwriting touch applies to the ~15–25% exception share (new-dealer, over-headroom, ineligible-category, and limit-review requests); ~25,000/yr → ~3,750–12,500 person-hours/yr (~8–25 hours/week), inside the dedicated Dealer Finance pod within the Finance & Accounting department envelope (§11.1's 53 HC covers Finance & Accounting + Internal Audit & Risk): Credit Manager 1 + Credit Analysts (Dealer Finance) 6–8 + Field Examiners 4–6 + program ops 1–2, ≈12–15 FTE of the AR/credit function; routine field exams beyond the in-house risk tier are contracted to third-party field-exam firms under VS-161, and disbursement processing rides shared VS-15 AP capacity).

steps.activity: Receive the dealer's funding request with the unit-level stocking list (SKU, serial/VIN/lot, cost).
Verify against the dealer's floor-plan limit and available headroom (W5370); check eligibility of categories.
Originate the floor-plan loan: principal, advance rate, curtailment schedule, rate (W5375), and RA 3765 disclosure (W5376).
Credit-decision per the authority matrix (CTL-12 separation); approve/decline with documented reason.
Release to disbursement (W5378) and post the loan to the floor-plan ledger (W5379).

workflows.name: Floor-Plan Disbursement to Vendor, Dual-Payee Check & Supplier Settlement

Automation Opportunity: - Disbursement auto-routed dual-payee; supplier invoice auto-marked floor-plan-paid.
Controls: - CTL-14/CTL-44 (duplicate-invoice/payment guard); CTL-10 (separate payment initiation from approval); CTL-21 (posting accuracy).
Cross-references: - links to VS-15 (P2P/AP), VS-18 (treasury/disbursement), VS-80 (payments), VS-17 (GL)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Diversion risk**: funds paid to the dealer (not the supplier) are diverted and not used to acquire collateral, leaving BuildRight unsecured; mitigated by dual-payee/direct-to-supplier disbursement.
- **Duplicate-payment risk**: paying a supplier invoice twice (origination + dealer's own payment); mitigated by 2-way/3-way match and clear-floor-plan-only payment marking.
System Touchpoints: - Disbursement/payment (VS-18/VS-80); AP (VS-15); floor-plan ledger principal posting; GL (VS-17).
Time Estimate: - Dual-payee generation, supplier settlement, and floor-plan-ledger posting are system-automated; the ~30–60-min manual touch (exception re-issuance, match breaks, proof-of purchase checks) applies to ~10–20% of ~25,000/yr → ~1,250–5,000 person-hours/yr (~3–10 hours/week), riding shared VS-15 AP capacity rather than dedicated headcount.

steps.activity: Generate the disbursement as a dual-payee instrument (BuildRight + dealer, or BuildRight + supplier) to ensure funds reach the supplier/stock.
Pay the supplier directly (or the dealer against proof of purchase) per the floor-plan structure.
Settle the supplier invoice (2-way/3-way match where applicable — VS-15) and clear the payable.
Post the disbursement to the floor-plan loan principal and the cash GL (VS-17/VS-18).
Confirm unit receipt by the dealer (triggering collateral registration W5379).

workflows.name: Unit-Level Collateral Registration, Serial/VIN Tracking & Floor-Plan Ledger Posting

Automation Opportunity: - Serial-level capture at dealer receipt auto-registers the collateral and posts the principal.
Controls: - CTL-795 (ensure controlled execution — Loan Origination, Disbursement & Inventory Collateral Tracking (PA-188.2).)
- operational: collateral-ledger accuracy; CTL-23 (OOT/fraud detection); CTL-26 (collateral registration).
Cross-references: - links to VS-05 (inventory), VS-35 (assets), VS-17 (GL), VS-23 (loss prevention)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Untracked-collateral risk**: a funded unit not registered at serial level cannot be curtailed or verified, enabling OOT; mitigated by mandatory serial-level registration before principal posting.
- **Reconciliation-gap risk**: funded units ≠ disbursement/invoice indicates leakage/fraud; mitigated by batch reconciliation.
System Touchpoints: - Floor-plan/collateral ledger (unit-level serial/VIN); loan principal posting; reconciliation vs. disbursement/invoice/receipt.

steps.activity: Capture unit-level collateral identity: SKU, serial/VIN/lot, cost, dealer, and loan reference.
Register the unit in the floor-plan/collateral ledger with BuildRight's security interest (W5371).
Post the funded unit to the dealer's floor-plan loan balance (principal).
Reconcile units funded ↔ disbursement ↔ supplier invoice ↔ dealer receipt.
Enable unit-level curtailment tracking and OOT detection (W5382/W5385).

fields.Trigger: Dealer transfers floor-planned units between locations/branches; third-party lien claim

workflows.name: Dealer Inventory Movement, Transfer & Subordinate-Lien Notification

Automation Opportunity: - Dealer-portal movement notification auto-updates the collateral ledger and flags off-premises moves.
Controls: - CTL-795 (ensure controlled execution — Loan Origination, Disbursement & Inventory Collateral Tracking (PA-188.2).)
Cross-references: - links to VS-100 (legal/liens), VS-68 (credit risk), VS-05 (inventory movement)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Lost-priority risk**: an undocumented transfer or unmanaged subordination subordinates BuildRight's security interest to another creditor; mitigated by movement-notification and lien-priority review.
- **Hidden-transfer risk**: a dealer moving units off-premises to evade audit/recovery; mitigated by movement-notification policy and field-exam verification (W5381).
System Touchpoints: - Collateral/lien register (unit-level); location update; legal/subordination records (VS-100).

steps.activity: Receive dealer notification of an inter-branch/unit transfer of floor-planned inventory.
Update the unit's location in the collateral ledger; preserve BuildRight's security interest across the move.
On any third-party (subordinate/junior) lien claim on a unit, assess and document priority / subordination agreement.
Confirm BuildRight's first-priority security interest is maintained or formally subordinated only with approval.
Update the collateral/lien register and dealer risk grade if subordination occurred.

fields.Trigger: Onboarding (W5372); periodic exam cycle; risk-triggered exam

workflows.name: Dealer Stocking-List Audit, Physical Inventory Verification & Field Examination

Automation Opportunity: - Risk-based exam scheduling from aging/OOT signals; mobile serial-scan app for field verification.
Controls: - CTL-795 (ensure controlled execution — Loan Origination, Disbursement & Inventory Collateral Tracking (PA-188.2).)
- operational: collateral-accuracy; CTL-23 (OOT/fraud detection); CTL-11 (separate counting from approval).
Cross-references: - links to VS-68 (credit), VS-21 (audit), VS-23 (LP), VS-161 (TPRM)
Pain Points / Risks: - **OOT-undetected risk**: infrequent or shallow exams let OOT accumulate into large unsecured exposure; mitigated by risk-based exam frequency and serial-level verification.
- **Dealer-obstruction risk**: a dealer obstructing the exam signals distress; mitigated by a right-to-examine clause and escalation to workout (W5386).
System Touchpoints: - Floor-plan/collateral ledger; field-exam findings register; risk-grade update; OOT-exception link (W5385).
Time Estimate: - ~1–3 person-days per exam, risk-tiered: the in-house Field Examiners (4–6) cover the high-risk tier (~600–900 exams/yr → ~900–2,700 person-days/yr); the routine quarterly tier of the ~3,000/yr cycle is contracted to third-party field-exam firms under VS-161 governance (dealer-charged or program-costed, not BuildRight headcount).

steps.activity: Schedule the exam (cycle or risk-triggered by aging/OOT flags from W5385).
Physically verify funded units on the stocking list (serial-level) against the floor-plan ledger.
Identify exceptions: missing units (sold OOT), damaged, or commingled with non-funded stock.
Require cure for exceptions (curtailment W5382, repayment, or collateral substitution); document.
Update the dealer risk grade and exam findings register; escalate repeat/serious exceptions.

fields.Trigger: Dealer reports a unit sold (or curtailment period expires)

workflows.name: Sold-Unit Reporting, Curtailment Schedule & Floor-Plan Paydown Processing

Automation Opportunity: - Dealer sold-unit feed auto-triggers curtailment and collateral release; auto-flag OOT exceptions.
Controls: - CTL-795 (ensure controlled execution — Loan Origination, Disbursement & Inventory Collateral Tracking (PA-188.2).)
- operational: curtailment accuracy; CTL-23 (OOT detection); CTL-20 (cash accountability).
Cross-references: - links to VS-16 (O2C/cash application), VS-68 (credit), VS-05 (inventory)
Pain Points / Risks: - **OOT risk**: a unit sold without curtailment within the period is the core floor-plan default vector; mitigated by sold-vs-curtailed matching and OOT-exception flagging.
- **Mis-application risk**: a curtailment payment applied to the wrong unit distorts the collateral ledger; mitigated by serial-level payment matching.
System Touchpoints: - Dealer inventory feed (W5374); floor-plan curtailment engine; cash application (VS-16); collateral release.

steps.activity: Receive dealer sold-unit report (from the inventory feed W5374 or manual) with the unit serial and sale date.
Match the sold unit to the funded collateral (W5379); compute the curtailment (principal + accrued interest) due.
Apply the dealer's curtailment payment to the specific unit's loan balance; release the collateral.
Flag units sold but not curtailed within the curtailment period → OOT exception (W5385).
Update the floor-plan ledger and dealer available headroom.

workflows.name: Floor-Plan Interest/Markup Accrual, Billing & Dealer Statement Generation

Automation Opportunity: - Fully automated accrual, subvention netting, statement generation, and GL posting.
Controls: - CTL-34: correct tax treatment on financing income; CTL-30 (month-end close — interest/markup accrual completeness).
Cross-references: - links to VS-16 (AR), VS-17 (GL), VS-157 (revenue recognition), VS-39 (subvention)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Accrual-error risk**: mis-keyed rates or balances produce incorrect statements and disputes; mitigated by automated accrual from the rate engine and ledger.

- **Revenue-misclassification risk**: floor-plan interest income vs. subvention vs. late fees must be correctly classified for tax (VAT/percentage tax) and PFRS; mitigated by defined GL mapping (VS-157).
System Touchpoints: - Floor-plan accrual/billing engine; AR (VS-16); GL posting (VS-17); revenue recognition (VS-157).
Time Estimate: - ~2 days elapsed per monthly cycle; ~1,000 statements.

steps.activity: Accrue interest/markup on each dealer's outstanding floor-plan balance at the contractual rate (W5375).
Compute subvention/manufacturer buy-down on eligible units (W5375) and net the dealer bill.
Generate the dealer statement: opening balance, fundings, curtailments, interest, subvention, and closing balance.
Post interest income and subvention to GL (VS-17/VS-157); issue the statement to the dealer.
Monitor collections against the statement (W5384) and aging (W5385).

workflows.name: Dealer Payment Processing, Cash Application & Loan Account Reconciliation

Automation Opportunity: - Auto-matching of bank remittance to units/statement; auto-update headroom.
Controls: - CTL-19: bank reconciliation; CTL-20 (cash accountability); CTL-21 (application accuracy).
Cross-references: - links to VS-16 (O2C/AR), VS-18 (treasury/cash), VS-17 (GL), VS-80 (payments)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Unapplied-cash risk**: payments not applied to the correct unit/statement distort curtailment and OOT detection; mitigated by remittance-detail matching and daily reconciliation.
- **Short-pay/dispute risk**: unresolved short-pays accumulate into delinquency; mitigated by timely dispute resolution and aging follow-up (W5385).
System Touchpoints: - Cash application/lockbox (VS-16/VS-18); floor-plan ledger reconciliation; bank reconciliation (VS-17 CTL-19).

steps.activity: Receive the dealer payment (bank transfer/check/e-wallet) and match to the dealer/statement.
Apply the payment: curtailment to specific units (W5382) or interest/statement (W5383) per remittance detail.
Reconcile the floor-plan loan account: payments vs. statement vs. ledger.
Investigate and resolve unapplied/short/over-payments and dealer disputes.
Update dealer available headroom and aging (W5385).
